candidate.answerReason: The combined travel is half a circumference at the first meeting and three halves at the second. Uniform speeds make the second meeting occur at three times the first meeting time, yielding circumference 480.

methods.label: Compare the first two meeting times
methods.explanation:
Starting at opposite points means the travelers first meet when their combined distance is half the circumference. After that meeting, their combined distance must increase by one full circumference before they meet again.

Let the circumference be \(C\) yards. The combined distances at the first and second meetings are therefore \(C/2\) and \(3C/2\). Their combined speed is constant, so the second meeting occurs at three times the elapsed time of the first. Each traveler has consequently gone three times as far.

At the first meeting, \(B\) has traveled \(100\) yards, so \(A\) has traveled \(C/2-100\) yards. At the second meeting, \(A\) is \(60\) yards short of a lap. Hence
\[
3\left(\frac C2-100\right)=C-60.
\]
Solving gives
\[
\frac{3C}{2}-300=C-60,
\qquad \frac C2=240,
\qquad C=480.
\]
For this circumference, \(A\) travels \(140\) yards before the first meeting and \(420\) before the second, leaving the required \(60\) yards. Thus the circumference is \(\boxed{480}\) yards, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
